title: The Crash
fluff:
“I still remember the light from the borealis on that night the satellites fell…”

-Excerpt from Jamie Nosek’s autobiography, ‘A Way Home’.
content:
In the early 2000s NASA and multiple other space agencies worldwide began to report abnormal sunspot readings. NASA had predicted that there would be increased sunspot activity due to the expected solar maximum. However, the readings reported in 2002 and 2003 were still far beyond initially expected. This news was quickly forgotten as none of the coronal mass ejections were planned to be on course for Earth, and it just became another fearmongering headline for an event that wouldn't happen.

In 2005, CNES reported even further increased sunspot activity and the statistics for what would happen if the Earth made contact with one. The report detailed a total communications blackout, mass destruction of infrastructure, and 'sending humanity to the Stone Age.' The international community again forgot this report, only for disaster to strike four years later.

In 2009, a Coronal Mass Ejection was reported on course for Earth and was predicted to affect Europe. Governments quickly formed plans in their 16 days of preparation, and they tried to keep control of the situation by not releasing the information to the public. On the 17th of April, the skies above Europe shone with bright, colorful lights as the solar storm hit. But the preparations were not enough. All of Europe was left without power for the next six months, wildfires from short-circuiting electronics in the Baltics clouded the skies of Europe with smog, and reparation costs exceeded 5 trillion (2022 USD) to bring power and satellite connection back to Europe. The blackout lasted over six months, ending in November of 2009. This event quickly led to other governments establishing procedures and plans if another one was on course to hit the Earth.

In the years that followed Black April, Europe was able to bounce back from the disaster, and the UN established 'tech vaults' to preserve electronics and equipment if a solar storm hit the Earth. These vaults were built mainly by countries that could afford the billions that went into creating these vaults. Still, some governments invested the money into other technologies to resist the storms, hoping they could get by with cost-effective solutions.

It would be more than half a decade later that humanities preparations would be put to the test. Researchers always warned of 'The Big One' as solar storms began to wane in the years following Black April, and sunspot activity only increased. In February of 2016, early warning satellites reported seeing 'The Big One.' With only 20 days to prepare, world governments moved quickly to preserve what they could and keep control of the situation.

Stay-behind forces in the conflict zones and overseas were quickly activated, countries scrambled to bring their people home, equipment was stuffed into tech vaults in hopes they would survive the coming storm, and satellites shifted into safe mode to weather it. However, when 'the big one' hit, and the skies above lit up with bright lights and showers of satellites, many of these plans quickly fell apart.

Most satellites were thrown into the expanse of space, power grids fried and caused fires, most of the internet went silent, and trillions of dollars in irreversible infrastructure damage was caused. The four years that followed were dubbed 'The Crash' on what remained of social networks.

For many, four years of The Crash were really two years of global networks being down, and then two more long years of reparations with constant shortages of food and civil unrest. But for soldiers, the situation was even more dire. Many stay-behind forces in the Middle-East and Africa were unable to establish contact with their command, and with rising tensions with locals, many units deserted to try and find their way home or survive the way they could best.

Many of these deserters turned to mercenary work for a living, taking contracts from whoever was giving in exchange for food and supplies. Others tried to navigate their way home, with a small group of four US marines circumnavigating Asia to get back to North America through Alaska. For those that stayed loyal, they were able to establish connection back to their countries early the next year, and provided as much aid as they could get. Which wasn’t much. The Global War on Terror was over by then, and the goal had shifted to bringing troops home.

title: Calamari Operational Support Group
fluff:
Anywhere, Anytime, Anyhow.

Calamari Operational Support Group draws upon a wide array of sources. Geographical Intelligence from satellites (GEOINT), Human Intelligence from the field (HUMINT), Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), along Open Source and Social media intelligence (OSINT) to ensure operational success anytime, anywhere. Our expert analysts and AI rapidly process and synthesize vast data, delivering near-real-time situational awareness directly applicable to our clients' needs. Empowering them to make informed, data-driven decisions in rapidly evolving environments.

However, our work doesn't end with Intelligence. We also provide risk management solutions, cybersecurity, asset protection, search and rescue, mine action, disaster response, advising, aggressor squadrons and direct intervention for our clients. Not to mention our work with in fighting forest fires and curbing the wild boar population.
content:
Calamari Operational Support Group is a PMC registered under the UNCC and founded by former CIA-SAC director Michael Calhoun in the late 90s. Initially, the company was called Basilisk Security Solutions and took contracts exclusively from the US, UK, and France. But after the 2005 Paris Accords, they began to expand their operations. Namely, the PMC started to participate in humanitarian operations, playing OPFOR during exercises, and advising. However, by 2010, the PMC was falling behind compared to others in the industry and had gone from 100,000 employees in 2006 to just shy of 20,000 by 2011 after biting off more than they could chew.

Though, the PMC would get bought out by Gold Coast Laboratories in 2011, a leading defense contractor for the US Military, and undergo a name change to Calamari Operational Support Group. No one truly knows why they decided to shift the name to be a dish of fried squid; some say it was a branding gimmick, others a practical joke, but the name and squid branding stuck. By 2012, the buyout was complete, and Calamari was now officially a subsidiary of Gold Coast.

As Gold Coast's subsidiary and in-house PMC, they provide security for their facilities and field-test emerging technologies. Advanced UAVs, UGVs, improved sensors, AI integration, Particle Refraction, and advanced Augmented Reality Displays to name a few. By 2014, Gold Coast had turned this small 20,000-man PMC into one of the most advanced fighting forces in the world, established almost complete dominance in the contracting industry, all while providing for 200,000 employees worldwide.

However, when The Crash hit, the PMC suffered a massive blow when thousands of their contractors overseas became mercenaries. Gold Coast’s monopoly on arms-tech was diminished as contractors traded equipment and secrets for supplies and money. Companies like The Bastogne-Martel Foundation fought tooth and nail for Gold Coast equipment, and went from small fry to their direct European competitor because of it. And before long, Gold Coast and Calamari’s technological edge had become blunt, they had near peers in the market.

Following the 2018 revision of the Paris Accords, Calamari was able to recuperate from their losses during the crash with legitimized mercs. Taking in thousands of former soldiers from all over the world as part of their amnesty from the UN, the company returned to almost pre-crash numbers. By 2020, they were 150,000 employees strong and taking the same variety of contracts they were before, while also branching out to work with the Department of Land Management in forest fires and curbing the boar population in Australia.

The motto their units always tout is to “never fight the fair fight”, and with billions of dollars of research and development, field testing, and manpower behind them, the PMC’s technological edge has never been sharper.

title: SYNTEK
fluff:
Simplifying Trauma Care

”At SYNTEK Medical Technologies- we believe that breakthrough medicines require unique delivery systems to reach their full potential and provide desired clinical outcomes.  For hundreds of years, methods of recovery and trauma care have remained mostly the same. Tourniquets, bandages, and weeks upon weeks of recovery and atrophy.

 Innovation is long overdue, and at SYNTEK- we aim to redefine trauma care and recovery”
content:
SYNTEK Medical Technologies is a British pharmaceutical research company, Founded by James Trent and Arthur Andersen in the early 2010s at Oxford University in the United Kingdom. The company is one of the earliest known corporations to specialize into Nanomachine research, bringing on Dr. Alessia Gazzola And Dr. Kei Katoka, the informal ‘godmother’ and ‘godfather’ of modern nanomachine treatment. 

SYNTEK develops a variety of products, namely focusing in on nanomachines and nanite treatment, but also creates medical equipment for military use. Their main product is ‘chrysalis’- named after the golden wool of greek mythology- that is intended for rapid recovery by using nanomachines as ‘contractors’ for the body to speed up healing and stop atrophy. Debuting in 2018, the product was one of the largest commercial successes in nanomachine research- and the first affordable nanomachine treatment available. 

Since then, the company has continued to be at the forefront of nanomachine research, with Dr. Kei Katoka leaving the company in 2015 to return to Japan and teach nanomachine development at the University of Tokyo. However- in that time the company has expanded to also encompass two new divisions. SYNTAC, and advanced prosthetics. 

SYNTAC was formed in early 2018 and was a project spearheaded by Andersen, much to the dismay of Trent. The focus of the program was to fill a gap in medicine in the contracting sphere, through offering privatized medical services for CASEVAC, Search and Rescue, and hostage rescue. This project eventually turned into an official PMC under the UNCC, and when the 2019 merger with Gold Coast was finalized- was implemented as a division of SYNTEK working closely with Calamari. Comprising of both paramedics and special operators, SYNTAC attach to other units across Calamari, UKSF, and SOCOM to conduct missions for clientele.

However- the Advanced Prosthetics division was something that Trent created with the help of Bernard Bouchard, a major investor into the company. Created to supplement the civilian research at Oxford, the division specialized into cutting edge prosthetics for veterans and others who lost limbs and hands. Prosthetic research and development is namely done jointly with Gold Coast’s robotic division in JTC Calhoun- in the Bouchard Nanomachine and Prosthetics Research Center.

title: Bastogne-Martel Foundation
fluff:
Modern battles begin on the waves

“Militaries of the world use the electromagnetic spectrum - essential and invisible- to detect, deceive and disrupt the enemy while protecting friendly forces. As modern threats get more technologically advanced, controlling the waves only becomes more essential.

Staying ahead in this era calls for new capabilities. BMF’s expertise in Electronic Warfare, Cyberwarfare, and electromagnetic systems spans all domains, land, sea, air, and space. BMF’s specialized, multi-domain systems provide clients the information they want and deny the enemy the information they need to provide an edge in any scenario.”
content:
The Bastogne-Martel Foundation is a French-Belgian electronics firm originally from Violot and founded in 1965. The foundation has been a significant player in developing military electronics for clients such as France, Belgium, and Germany and was a pivotal contributor to the FELIN program, modernizing the French armed forces at the turn of the century. However, following The Crash and the boom in the PMC industry, this French-Belgian electronics firm began to stake its claim in the contracting market, bringing its cutting-edge electronics with it. Little is known about their in house PMC, ‘Orchestra’, but what is known is that they poach SOF from French, Belgian, Canadian, and Swiss units exclusively.

Rumors have it that Orchestra works closely with the United Nations to hunt down illegal mercenaries and takes ‘under the table’ contracts from MI6 and the DGSE. However, other rumors have also said that Orchestra has taken illegal contracts from the black market. Sabotage, assassination, kidnapping, along with skirting the 2005 Paris Accords to illegally operate where they aren’t supposed to. But that’s rumors between contras.

In the Underground, the name ‘Bastogne-Martel’ is met with fear and worry. The mere mention of the company turns confidence in a plan to concern. With a now disclosed 98% capture rate in an audit conducted by the UNCC in 2021, most of the underground stand to lose whenever they are known to be in an area, some remarking them as bogeymen and cancelling plans entirely just to avoid a capture. 

But again- rumors. Nothing has been confirmed- but it’s silently known that they exist in the underground as a means of hunting down mercs high up on the blacklist.

title: Ishida Heavy Industries
fluff:
We deliver innovative solutions to the world's toughest challenges.


"Fast-moving threats require agile deterrence with compatible platforms. IHI doesn’t just provide an updated system, but a new standard of architecture and open-system integration. Our allied partners require deterrence platforms that are interoperable and networked into an ecosystem designed for a new standard of connected protection.

Because connected systems save seconds when seconds matter most.

In an uncertain and volatile world, a strong defense industry requires anti-fragility – investing ahead of need to ensure production of critical security systems that can withstand disruptions and thrive in the face of adversity."
content:
Initially creating cruise ships and ferries, Ishida Heavy Industries was established in 1949 following the Second World War by Hoshino Ishida and his brother, Kazama. At first the humble company worked to create ferries and boats for fishermen, but slowly began to branch out towards other sectors as the company grew in size and manpower. By the turn of the century, Ishida Heavy Industries was one of the most significant names in Japan, alongside Mitsubishi, in defense. Developing mainly maritime equipment and unique vehicles on a license from other countries, Ishida began to grow more Indigenous projects following The Crash in 2016 and the 20 billion dollar grant to create tech vaults in the years before to preserve electronics before further solar storms hit the earth.

Following the crash, Ishida converted these tech vaults into RnD facilities to develop emerging technologies into equipment for the JSDF. Working closely with the Japanese Government, most of Ishida’s indigenous projects were focused on defending the country. From missile defense systems, Jamming, EW defense, and digital intrusion countermeasures, Ishida’s main goal was to defend Japan by providing its defenders with the cutting edge they’d need for any threat that arose.

Though, Ishida doesn’t work soley in defense. Ishida has multiple subsidiaries working in various sectors and still creates cruise liners and ferries.

As of 2022, the company has publicly stated that they have had a growing interest in large language models and machine learning, and leaks from inside the company suggest that their AI is making their higher-ups question if a machine can be ‘sentient’.

title: Gold Coast Laboratories
fluff:
We’re Defeating Tomorrow’s Threats, Today

”As domains merge and connect, new threats and opportunities arise.  By giving our clients every advantage for success, Gold Coast Laboratories is creating a safer world for everyone. This is the mission drives our innovation in robotics, medical, and defense technologies.

It’s a relentless pursuit of progress that drives us forward daily- because our progress matters. And it matters as what we deliver protects and connects our world one innovation at a time. By asking the hard questions in our research labs, engineering hubs, and on the field, our engineers and researchers push the envelope of what’s possible tomorrow to today. Because progress isn’t automatic- it’s initiated.

Progress defines the future- and it defines us at Gold Coast Laboratories.”
content:
Gold Coast Laboratories is a US-based defense contractor founded in 1987 by disgruntled Raytheon engineers Robert Coomer and Jacob Cross when their project to modernize the infantryman was canceled. They took the project and their team of engineers with them to San Francisco’s Silicon Valley to create Gold Coast Laboratories. Like The Bastogne-Martel Foundation, Gold Coast was paramount in the US’s Land Warrior program and pioneered the concept of Augmented Reality Displays. With their foot in the door, Cross, and Coomer then expanded Gold Coast to other sectors, namely robotics, avionics, and electronic warfare technologies.

By the early 2000s, Gold Coast was supplying Green Berets with the bleeding edge of the Land Warrior project to overwhelming success and reception from 5th SFG, 1btn, Delta Company. Enough that Gold Coast received funding to improve it as the technology trickled out to other units within US SOCOM.

In 2011, Gold Coast laboratories bought out Calamari OSG, formerly Basilisk SMG, to field test their equipment and provide security for their facilities. By 2020, this PMC had shifted to take on contracts for the US, UK, and the United Nations as one of the largest PMCs in the market, with 200,000 personnel from security and aviators to advisors and cyber warfare specialists. Calamari provides a range of services to clients, but namely provides personnel detail, direct action, advising, and plays OPFOR at their facility- JTC Monroe- in the mountains of Washington. Rumors have said that the CEO of Calamari, Michael Calhoun, has connections to the CIA- but those are just rumors.

Gold Coast since then moved on to develop further technologies for their in-house PMC and the US and UK armed forces. And as of 2021, the company has also brought in a few subsidiaries. Namely SYNTEK Medical Technologies to conduct nanite and prosthetic research, Bushmaster and Z&M to develop firearms technologies, and TurtleShell Dynamics for manufacturing specialized armor systems.

title: SAPP
fluff: [South American Prosperity Pact]
content:
SAPP (South American Properity Pact) Is an economic-security alliance formed between south american powerhouses in the early 2000s to deal with a growing cartel and drug crisis. Originally comprising of Chile, Brazil, and Argentina, the alliance started out as a 'five eyes' style alliance before shifting to also become an economic alliance after the Crash in 2016, where they nationalized their lithium mines and began to exert their influence onto the rest of South America. 

With a weakened United States, the rest of the world was forced to play ball with them and establish good relations due to the desperate need of lithium for modern electronics and the collapse of lithium mining operations in Africa. They were quick to bring their economy out of the red during the crash, and became an economic powerhouse on par with the United States, Europe, and China.

By 2019, the SAPP had began to encompass almost all of South America, with the leaders of the SAPP agreeing on a long term goal of reinforcing border strength and extending their outreach and anti-cartel operations north, while focusing on the short term goals of building political and economic unity. 

However, this goal would also be added with expansion into Africa in 2022, with SAPP starting to work on securing further lithium and reaching contention with Russian mercenary companies establishing the ‘power belt’, a belt from Kazakhstan to South Africa rich in lithium and uranium ores.

Notably, in 2018, a team of astronauts crash landed in the country and were reportedly taken by cartels, leading to the formation of Task Force Gold, who moved into the country to rescue them.

title: NATO
fluff: [North Atlantic Treaty Organization]
content:
The North Atlantic Treaty Organization, or Organisation du traité de l'Atlantique Nord, is an intergovernmental military alliance between 32 member states. 30 in Europe, and 2 in North America. Founded in the aftermath of the second world war, NATO was established with the signing of the North Atlantic treaty in 1949. The organization serves as a measure of collective security, where its independent member states agree to mutual defense in response to an attack by any external party, enshrined into Article 5 of the treaty: “an armed attack against one member shall be considered an attack against them all.”

Throughout the cold war, NATO’s main purpose was to deter and counter the threat posed by the soviet union and the satellite states that formed the Warsaw pact after 1955. However, with the dissolution of the soviet union in 1991, the organization shifted direction and conducted its first major interventions into Bosnia and Yugoslavia. And not soon after in 2001, Article 5 was invoked after the September 11th attacks, leading to the deployment of forces to afghanistan as part of ISAF (International Security Assistance Force). 

Since the turn of the century, NATO has been involved in a range of roles, from intervention, to training, to counter piracy, and more. But in more recent times- these tasks have fallen to contras.

However- following the crash in 2016, the alliance has become increasingly strained with policy shifts in multiple of the major powers. Countries like the United States have shifted stance to become more isolationist, only providing <1% of their GDP towards the NATO Readiness effort, alongside the UK who has sought to distance themselves from European authority, and similarly have redistributed their 5% GDP to only .3% of their GDP- the rest going towards their own armed forces and shifting towards AUSCANZUKUS. Canada similarly has followed suit with the rest of the commonwealth. 

European Powers on the other hand have struggled to keep NATO afloat against an increasingly irredentist Russia and a rising China. CSTO has grown to also encompass the Balkans, with certain members of the Balkan pact striking deals with Russia, and Turkey has left the alliance altogether due to worries of instability and a policy shift within the country. However- Poland, France, and Italy have all stepped up in an attempt to stabilize the alliance and fill the gaps that Canada, The United States, and the UK have left.

title: CSTO
fluff: [Collective Security Treaty Organization]
content:
Formed after the fall of the Warsaw Pact and the Soviet Armed Forces, the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO), or Organizatsiya dogovora o kollektivnoy bezopasnosti (ODKB), is an intergovernmental military alliance in Eurasia consisting of multiple post-Soviet states such as Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan, while also extending further south towards countries in the Middle East such as Iran, and then into North Africa along the power belt on the west coast. Notably, the former NATO state of Turkey had joined the alliance as well in 2019

The CSTO is similar to the North Atlantic Treaty and the Inter-American treaty in that they have its own Article 5, namely Article 4, where an act of aggression against one signatory would be perceived as an aggression against all. In 2002, the CSTO charter reaffirmed the desire of all participating states to abstain from the use or threat of force, while also prohibiting joining other military alliances. They have been a part of a wide range of roles. Namely, using their military force for counter-insurgency, counter-terrorism, fighting transnational crime, and providing safety and stability to member states via troop deployments from their internal Peacekeeping force and Collective Rapid Reaction Force. Though not as extensively as that of NATO.

Though, Come the turn of 2016 and the start of the Crash, the CSTO did not fare well alongside NATO. With a severe hit to global infrastructure and military power- as trillions of dollars worth of military equipment was turned into dead metal- Member states strained the alliance in an attempt to keep the situation under control. In 2017, when Siberia seceded from Russia to establish relations with the United States and the United Kingdom, the situation grew even more dire. With Russia losing over half its landmass and oil reserves, the alliance was almost dead in the water and failing to rebuild. 

However, with a landslide election in 2018 towards an irredentist government, a focus shift occurred internally from siphoning oil from what wells remained towards autonomous mass production and design of weapons and equipment. This shift, along with an open sales policy for export equipment, led to a large amount of Russian-designed weapons and gear winding up in the dark markets of the Underground, where they were discreetly sold to mercenaries and criminal organizations. With this boom in economics and weapons production came a boom in their use of PMCs to establish control of regions. Specifically, the power belt where the PMC Dryga has been used to secure large quantities of Lithium and Uranium. Due to this, and remnants of West African nations joining the CSTO in a bid for stability, they have turned from the sparks of old animosities to an encroaching housefire spanning from Central Asia, to Western Africa, and up to Eastern Europe.

title: Chinese Presidential Crisis
fluff:
“According to overseas reports, Chinese Navy Admiral Yuan has come into office after the prior president ‘resigned’ overnight. Further reports have detailed that Yuan has began a purge of the Chinese government, and many officials were moved to the kunlun mountains and replaced.” 

-CIA Classified documents, dated 5/2/17
content:
The Chinese National Crisis is an event that is oddly, poorly documented in the 21st century. Not much is known about the rapid transfer in power that occurred sometime in 2017, but the events that followed spiraled into a second cold war between NATO and China that lasted until 2024.

What is known, is that sometime in 2017 PLAN Admiral Yuan staged a military coup against the former president. The Chinese were not affected as badly by the solar storm due to the rapid construction of tech-vaults around the country, and were relatively stable compared to other countries around the world. This military coup was swift, and the shift in power took only a day until news came out of the assassination of the president by most of the cabinet. Yuan then stepped into power, and almost all of the cabinet in Shanghai were arrested and sent to the Kunlun mountains. 

Following the event, the Chinese government’s policies began to become more expansionist. The PLAN moved to control the South China sea and staged a 1 day invasion of Taiwan. The small country was overwhelmed and immediately put under martial law. 

By 2018, China was now the leading provider of microprocessors and semiconductors. Leading to concerns from the United States and other countries as China grew evermore expansionist in its policies. Some rumors say that they were the ones who stirred dissent and started the Japanese Civil War, but no founding evidence has come forth.

title: Chilean Astronaut Crisis
fluff:
“We’ll need a small team. Eight people at most, preferably with experience in these sorts of environments. Probably a HALO drop from an airliner moving into the country or they go in as tourists, and we’ll have CIA funnel the rest of their gear into safehouses in country for them.  They’ll need to know the risks, this mission is to be as clandestine as we can make it, if even one of them gets caught, this could spell war or worse- the SAPP now have even more leverage against us”

-Johnathan Berkeley, Transcript during the planning stages of Operation Silent Arrow.
content:
During re-entry from satellite restoration operations in 2018, a shuttle carrying ten astronauts had an fault and was sent off course to the coast of Chile.  When they landed, they were reportedly rescued by Cartels according to SAPP (South American Prosperity Pact) sources, and operations began in Chile by SAPP SOF to find these astronauts.

However, what wasn’t known was that the astronauts that were taken ransom by SAPP as retaliation and leverage after one of their industry spies were caught in the United States. Relations between the SAPP and the United States began to falter and was only furthered with the SAPP taking the eight astronauts hostage. Neither side wanted war, however neither side wished to let go of their leverage.

This then sparked the creation of Task Force Gold, a small task force comprising of remnants of NATO SOF. This team drew from CIA-SAD, SRR, SAS, SBS, Delta Force, 4e RPIMA, Green Berets, and other tier one units, borders and protocols ignored to bring these astronauts home. The operation started on the 20th of October, and was primarily headed by Mi6 and CIA who were working around the clock to find the astronauts, with Gold Coast and Bastogne Martel providing specialized top of the line equipment to the team.

title: The Paris Accords
content:
The 2005 Paris Accords was a charter signed by 187 countries, including France, Russia, the UK, and the United States, to 'legitimize' the use of PMCs in the 21st century. The charter outlined the purpose of PMCs, and defined the terms 'Mercenary' and 'Contractor' as two different terms for illegal independents and recognized PMCs.

The Paris Accords laid down a framework for PMCs to receive contracts through the United Nations Contracting Council (UNCC), Established strict oversight from world governments and NGOs, implemented harsher punishments for crimes, and allowed them to purchase  vehicles and military equipment from nations and companies. These accords let PMCs like Calamari expand and have a standing army with tanks, APCs, fighters, and more for their operations. In addition, when a PMC is registered under the UNCC, it can now be contracted by a nation to participate in a conflict in which the country is involved. This was used during the 2021 Siberian Nuke Crisis, where Calamari was contracted by the Siberian government to assist with retrieving three lost nukes from ultranationalists. But most of the time these PMCs are contracted by NGOs for security, Nations for personnel retrieval, or Militaries for advising and interdiction.

On the other side, the charter also declared that independent mercenaries were illegal, and mercenary groups were to register with the United Nations to become PMCs during the amnesty period lasting until 2006. Due to the nature of only being able to accept contracts through the UNCC, many independents and mercenaries didn't become 'legitimate' and continued to operate illegally. However, with their status as illegal, the UN provided bounties for independent and mercenary groups, leading to their decline over the coming years as the jobs became more and more dangerous with PMCs always on the lookout for a bounty to hunt while on the job.

It wouldn't be until 2018 that the United Nations would come back and change the Paris Accords to introduce a revised amnesty program. With the number of deserters during the crash who found work as mercenaries numbering in the thousands, the UN couldn't enforce The Paris Accords, and mercenaries were running rampant in the Middle East and Africa. The UN then introduced 'legitimizing,' where independents and mercenary groups could be given conditional amnesty. However, depending on their actions as a mercenary, they were sometimes denied this amnesty. Those granted it were given the option of signing on with a PMC like Bastogne-Martel's Orchestra or Gold Coast's Calamari, or laying down their arms for good and returning to civilian life with all charges dropped. The program was successful, and thousands of mercenaries entered the amnesty program to lay down their arms or sign on with a PMC. This program ran until 2020, where mercs that surrendered continued to be put on trial, with rare cases of amnesty for not turning themselves in earlier.

For those that remained mercenaries, the UN introduced bounties for known mercs that PMCs could pursue. Some PMCs, such as Bastogne-Martel worked closely with the United Nations to bring these mercenaries in, usually for substantial compensation. But for those that have stood the test of time, they’ve proven themselves to be elusive targets, with ever increasing bounties on their heads to bring them in to atone for their crimes.

title: The Underground
fluff: "They're essentially a cabal of syndicates, mafias, yakuzas, and triads. Whole motto is basically being a thieves guild, but for the worst of the worst." - CLMRI ISR Report, 12/2/2020
content:
Originally created in the early 90s by criminal syndicates in Europe, The Underground is a network of hired assassins, hitmen, fixers, smugglers, and more unsavory types. They provide jobs for independent mercs and mercenary groups, help move equipment for deals and sales, and then also take care of the more ‘problematic types’ in the industry for the highest bidders. They are reminiscent of a thieves guild in organization. Decentralized, but interconnected and with honor among them and their respective parties. 

The Underground is theorized to span from the Italian Mafias of New York, to the Triads in Hong Kong. Jobs flow freely through the underground, with fixers organizing missions for the clients, and mercs finishing the job. 

During The Crash, The Underground boomed with thousands of mercs becoming a part of the underground looking for jobs, supplies, fixers, and equipment. While the rest of the world was struggling to bring itself back to it’s feet, they took the opportunity to expand and develop the network into the underground cabal that it is today. 

However, in 2018 after the revision to the Paris Accords, The Underground took a massive hit with hundreds of thousands of mercs turning ‘legit’, their term for receiving amnesty and returning to civilian life or joining a legitimate PMC. This was furthered with the creation of ‘The Blacklist’, which led to Calamari OSG, Bastogne Martel’s Orchestra, and a NATO Task Force starting to hunt down the most prolific and infamous mercenaries in The Underground.

By 2022, The Underground still exists as a means of mercenaries to find jobs, buy arms through the black market, and move around the world discreetly. However it is not at the peak it was during The Crash

title: The Blacklist
fluff: "He's the numba fifteen guy on the blacklist-" Number 19, seconds before capture during a DGSE sting operation.
content:
The Blacklist is a UNCC controlled list of all known mercenaries currently active within the underground. 

Dubiously dubbed ‘The Blacklist’ by the mercenaries on it, the collection of mercenaries is effectively a bounty board of some of the most prolific and notable mercenary groups and individuals in the world. hitmen, fixers, assassins, and more all with a bounty on their head following the ratification of the revision to the UN Paris Accords in 2018.

The Blacklist is kept track of by various intelligence agencies within the UN, including Mi6, FBI, DGSE, and CIA who all frequently monitor the list and increase bounties as targets become more and more dangerous or infamous. 

Frequently, Private Military Companies will hunt down members of these blacklists as they show up, namely Calamari OSG, who deploy their Special Reconaissance Groups, or Bastogne Martel who frequently deploy their in house unit, Orchestra, to hunt down these mercenaries and bring them in-front of the ICC.

The top fifteen are considered some of the top mercenaries in the world, and are hard to find. However, they also have the largest payout if brought in dead or alive. In the underground, it’s a status symbol to become one of these top fifteen, while in the contracting sphere it’s an achievement to hunt one down and bring them in-front of the ICC alive.

Following the aftermath of the 2018 revisions, Calamari OSG and Orchestra both joined with a NATO Task Force to eliminate the top twenty of this blacklist in a clean sweep, bringing in or killing hundreds of mercs in the underground and dealing a hard blow to the underground in an attempt to curb the mercenary industry in Africa and the Middle East.

title: Contras And Mercs
content:
The terminology of ‘Contra’ and ‘Merc’ can both tied back to their original words and their classifications under the UN’s 2005 Paris Accords.

‘Contra’ is a shortened version of “Contratista” the translation of ‘contractor’ into Spanish. The term originally comes from the SAPP, where in the early 2000’s contractors from the United States could be found in South America doing ‘wetwork’. It also was a dual meaning with the anti-Marxist group also sharing the same name. However, in modern times the term is just meant to refer to Contractors as a whole. Contractors are personnel of PMCs registered under the United Nations Contracting Council (UNCC), such as Calamari, or Orchesta.

Meanwhile, the term ‘Merc’ is just shorthand for Mercenary. However, it carries with it a negative connotation due to the status of Mercenaries under the Paris Accords. Mercenaries are illegal independents or groups of independents that aren’t registered under the UNCC. Due to their illegal nature, they also undertake illegal contracts, usually from The Underground. The most prolific of these mercs are a part of the UNCC’s ‘Blacklist’, a list containing the top 15 most wanted mercenaries in the world.

However, there are also ‘Legitimized’ Mercs. These are former mercs who turned themselves into the ICC, and were provided amnesty following the 2018 revisions of the Paris Accords. These contractors may have officially severed their ties to The Underground, but many still keep close contacts and have favors still left to cash in, or vice versa.

Usually, these two groups are always at odds with one another. With contractors being provided bonuses for bringing in mercs dead or alive, with mercs receiving no benefit for hunting down contractors. Unless they’re legitimized and owe something to someone in The Underground.

title: Charlie's Devils
content:
Charlies Devils were an infamous group of mercenaries that operated from late 2016 to early 2018, and were a notable group of the Underground in the middle east before they vanished in January of 2018 when the group was designated a part of ‘The Blacklist’

From what little records and notes from Fixers and contacts in the underground mention, they were a team of UKSF of some variety. Each with differing devil masks with horns attached to them. Notably, fixers commented that the one with a silver mask the leader, and the one with a yellow mask and a wide smile was their 2IC.

The group was infamous for their work in the Arabian Peninsula. The ‘Qatar Job’ and ‘Dubai job’ being their most infamous where they stole hundreds of millions of dollars worth in gold and riches in Qatar, while in Dubai they stole from the Emirati royalty.  They also operated elsewhere in the Horn of Africa and even up to Syria with what some fixers have mentioned.

However, their jobs would end in January of 2018, when the UN ratified the revisions for the Paris Accords and the Blacklist was formed. Mysteriously, over the span of that month, they disappeared entirely from Underground Circles. Some rumors state that PMCs took the opportunity to hunt them down, others say the Emiratis put a bounty on them discreetly, but what is known is their legacy through the formation of copycat groups looking to reach their level of fame and infamy. Each with their own copycat theming, usually being animals, clowns, or other similar themes.

title: The Power Belt
content:
Created after the crash by the Russian PMC Dryga Corp, the Power Belt is a supply line from the southernmost tip of Africa all the way up to Kazakhstan and CSTO controlled territory.

The Power Belt was created due to an increasing demand for lithium to create new electronics, and with the current leading provider being the SAPP, The Russian Federation wanted to secure their own lithium during the chaos of the crash using Dryga Corp as security for the route.

Officially coined as the region encompassing Kazakhstan, the Horn of Africa, and the eastern seaboard of Sub-Saharan Africa, Dryga Corp maintain outposts along the route for shipments of Uranium and Lithium back to Russia and CSTO aligned nations.

However, this is being encroached on by the SAPP, who by 2022 have begun to establish control in the region in attempts to monopolize the lithium industry.

title: Augmented Reality Displays
content:
In the late 80’s the United States military was looking to create the ‘Soldier Of The Digital Era’. What they envisioned was using a combination of commercial and current-issue military equipment to integrate small arms with digital displays, provide command and control at infantry levels, and look at the individual soldier as a complete unit rather than as a segment of a larger force. The program went unnamed at first, and was initially given to Raytheon … Who then had to pull from the program prematurely even with promising results that were almost a decade ahead of its time. The project was binned, and almost forgotten if not for Raytheon engineers Robert Coomer and Jacob Cross. 

Coomer and Cross quickly left Texas for the Silicon valley, along with a large chunk of their intial team, to continue where they left off. By the end of 1999, they approached the United States Army with initial prototypes of what would become of the Land Warrior system. And one 50 million dollar grant, eight years, and the creation of Gold Coast Laboratories later, the first generation Land Warrior system was officially complete.

The initial Land Warrior system fulfilled the concept of computerizing the future soldier. The initial design was based off of monocle HUDs used by helicopter pilots, but was smaller and more powerful. The monocle display provided navigation and waypoint markers via a compass at the top of their view, and connected via satellite to military LAN/WAN networks for improved command and control. A rough implementation of the BFTC, or Blue Force Tracker Chip that was attached to friendly gear, allowed the soldier to rapidly identify friendlies when they came into their line of sight. As long as the chip was on them. 

These first generation Land Warrior systems were fielded by 5th Special Forces Group and tested rigorously up to 2000. Following 9/11, they would quickly be put to the test in the hands of Task Force Dagger to resounding success. Other countries also founded their own programs, such as the French FELIN program which also aimed to computerize their forces, but also included displays for thermal, and linked to the weapon’s optic.

As The Global War On Terror continued, these first generation systems would be pushed to their limits. By 2009, the monocles were updated one last time to include a round counter, improved IFF tracking, and also to show the conditions of fellow soldiers using the BFTC. These systems would quickly trickle down from the Green Berets and Delta down to the Ranger Regiment, as second generation systems were developed by Bastogne-Martel and Gold Coast. 

The second generation systems went by a new name. In the United States, it was the ‘Future Force Warrior’ program. In Russia, it was “Ratnik’. Either way- the second generation took what was learned from Land Warrior and Felin, and added more. In the American Future Force Warrior program, Gold Coast took heavy inspiration from Halo and Modern Warfare to construct a UI interface that was more intuitive and akin to a ‘video game’. Bastogne-Martel, did the same. As well, 3d images could be produced by a low-intensity laser projecting them through the pupil and onto the retina. And lastly, hardened uplinks and downlinks allowed for direct connections to drones, allied vehicles, and more for better command and control. Usually, these second generation systems came in the form of goggles, and still required a helmet attachment for the mini-computer, but they could now mount night vision systems simultaneously.

These systems would quickly be fielded By Delta Force, and were notable for their use by NAVY SEALs during the Osama Bin Laden raid. As before, these systems trickled down to other units as newer versions were bought and fielded.

By 2016 however, many of these systems would break and burn during the Crash. And with rising costs for electronic components across the board- they have only been seen in the hands of select SOF units. But there are rumors of Gold Coast and Bastogne-Martel providing their in-house contractors with third generation systems… What these look like? It’s been well guarded, but one can speculate.

title: Artificial Intelligence
content:
Artificial intelligence is at it’s core, ‘artificial’. It is matrices upon matrices, algorithms inside algorithms, all to predict what is the next likely best word in a sentence. It is essentially spamming autocorrect over and over again, except you get a coherent answer. 

AI originally saw it’s big debut with Siri in 2008, and then quickly became more and more powerful as more research and money was invested into it. Come 2013, AI was one of the largest industries in the United States, for better or worse. While it did make jobs, it also took many- and while it made writing and creating content easier- it also put out fake information. it created a negative recursive loop- where one source would use AI, get false information, and then post it onto the internet only for another to see it. Turning what was fake and misconstrued ideas into supposed facts online within two years. 

Come 2015, most academics saw online resources as easily fake. Which led to libraries and books becoming the new ‘net’ of sorts. And when the solar storms of 2016 arrived- the old net was wiped clean. Most AIs and models never followed into the post-crash world, and with strict regulation appearing in the EU and US under Bartlett’s administration, the AI boom slowed down drastically. 

However- AI research is still underway. As an academic tool for research, AI has unprecedented access to research and studies to draw conclusions from. But more recently- companies such as Gold Coast and Ishida have been studying their uses for military use. Coordinating units in the event of a loss of chain of command, filing and completing paperwork to speed up bureaucracy, and in Calamari’s case- an on field assistant to relay and synthesize data and information on command.

title: Supersonic Highways
content:
Developed in the early 2000s, Supersonic highways were an advent of Gold Coasts and Boeing’s Mach Cutoff program. The program tested the concept of high altitude mach cutoffs, where at a certain speed and with certain atmospheric conditions, sonic booms could refract in atmosphere and never be audible to anyone on the ground.

The system relied on experimental and state of the art, multi-core processors from Intel that used telemetries on the local atmosphere to adjust the speed in real time so the refraction effect could occur. When debuted in 2000, and with a bit of lobbying, the creation of the supersonic international highway was ratified by the UN, creating high altitude supersonic corridors over the seven seas.

title: General Security Forces
fluff: SecFor/G-SEC
content:
General Security Forces, or ‘GSF’ is the internal name used to define everyone ranging from their tip of the spear Special Reconnaissance Groups, to the logicians managing requisitions to keep everyone fed and happy. The GSF does have a few notable units however:

>The Rapid Response Regiment, also known as R3 or Triple R.
    - Serves as main offensive fighting force, split into three major battalions, and also includes the Special Purpose Battalion. Commonly referred to as troopers on the field.

>Long Range Reconaissance Company
    - Part of the Special Purpose Battalion in the R3 regiment, they do what is on the tin. Long range reconaissance, support, and intelligence gathering. Commonly referred to as Beekeepers for their mesh veil over boonie cap.

>SYNTAC AMS
    - Part of SYNTEK, SYNTAC are the companies’ premiere pararescue jumpers and paramedics. Referred to as Blackberry, Blueberry, or Winterberry by what color of poncho they wear.

>Cyber Exploitation Group
   - Part of the Special Purpose Battalion, CYEX is a specialized Signal and Cyberwarfare Group focused around preserving Calamari’s Datalink connection, and exploiting the enemy’s. 

>Hazardous Environment Assault Team
   - Part of the Special Purpose Battalion, HEAT are CBRN and EOD specialists tasked with operating in hazardous exclusion zones to rout targets and mercenaries using those areas to hide.

>Special Reconaissance Detachment
   - Formed from the Long Range Reconaissance Company, the SRD is it’s own unit outside of the R3 regiment’s structure. It is split into three groups, with small teams of 5-10 in each that are tasked with high risk direct action operations and the tip of the spear.

title: Rapid Response Regiment
fluff: R3/RRR/"Troopers"
content:
Organized similarly to the 75th Rangers or a Marine MEU, the Rapid Response Regiment consists of infantry reinforced with artillery, tanks, armored vehicles, combat engineers, reconnaissance, and other units as the mission and circumstances require. the total strength is split between 5 Battalions, each with ~1,400 members each and ~7000 members overall.

-1st Battalion 

-2nd Battalion 

-3rd Battalion

-Special Purpose Battalion

-Headquarters Battalion

1st, 2nd, and 3rd battalions are all organized to include a Ground Combat Element, and a Logistics Combat Element.

The GCE is the Battalion’s main fighting force. It conducts offensive, defensive, and stability operations, including amphibious assaults, raids, and combat in urban or rugged environments. It includes infantry, artillery, armor, reconnaissance, and engineers. 

Meanwhile the LCE ensures the GCE have what they need to operate effectively. This includes logistics, supply, transportation, medical support, maintenance, and engineering. The LCE sustains the Battalion’s operations by keeping troops equipped, vehicles running, and supplies flowing.

The Special Purpose Battalion on the other hand is comprised of specialized units for the Regiment’s combat operations. Such as the Long Range Reconnaissance Company (LRRC) who specialize into weeks long reconnaissance missions deep behind enemy lines, or the Cyber Exploitation Group (CYEX) who provide both cyber defense and exploitation.

title: Special Reconaissance Detachment
fluff: SRD/SRG
content:
The Special Reconnaissance Detachment was a unit originally from the Special Purpose Battalion, but turned into it’s own division in 2019 after the need for a dedicated special mission unit was found during an operation in Indonesia in that same year. The group represents Calamari’s tip of the spear, and fills in the gap for counterterrorism, hostage rescue, special reconnaissance, and direct action. Often against high-value targets. The SRG is split into three groups, with their own teams inside to fit specific mission requirements. 

-1st Special Reconnaissance Group (Airborne) 
-2nd Special Reconnaissance Group (Maritime)
-3rd Special Reconnaissance Group (RnD)

Each Group comprises of at least 5-6 tightly knit teams inside with a headquarters element included. Though, 3rd Special Reconaissance Group notably is only 2 teams. Gambler, and Mobster, with a headquarters element. And unlike the other groups, 3rd SRG is used an RnD watershed for emerging technologies before they trickle out to the rest of the SRD and R3.

Selection for SRG teams is a lengthy process and starts with applications. Most who even get a response back are either referred internally from the PMC, have an extensive background in SOF, or are members of R3 looking for the next leg up. Once the applications are sifted through by recruiters, they then bring the applicants to the ‘Weedout’ as it’s referred to in company. The Weedout is an 13 week selection/training process that occurs at every base that Calamari has a presence and authorization to conduct selection in. The Weedout itself is rigorous and intended to whittle the crowd of applicants best they can, and is heavily based off of the LRRC’s own selection and training. By the end, there are approximately 20 trainees, all of which are sent to JTC Calhoun for the final selection.

During final selection, recruits are placed into what will become their Special Reconaissance Team, and given a number. They are only to be referred to by that number, and if someone is referred to by name, the entire team is collectively disqualified. At the end of final selection, the team will then be interviewed by another active team within their already assigned Special Reconaissance Group. Usually if applicants get this far, it is a means of other members of the team to get to know the new faces joining them, and usually ends with the recruits being given their Special Reconaissance tab.

title: Long Range Reconaissance Company
fluff: LRRC/"Beekeepers"
content:
Highly decorated and known as the ‘beekeepers’ for their mesh and boonies, LRRC are tasked with providing worldwide reconnaissance and operational preparation in support of other units within the GSF or occasionally USSOCOM and UKSF. Originally the LRRC was divided into nine two-man teams, three teams to support each of the three Rapid Response Battalions. However with an increase in contracts, this number has increased to approximately 18. The unit has three primary tasks: Active Reconnaissance, Surveillance, and Direct Action.

Each team is headed usually by a Staff Sergeant, known as the TL. There are approximately nine teams within the company . All nine maintain at least four to eight personnel each. The company itself is directed by their battalion headquarters section.

Training and selection requires all candidates completing a selection process including navigation from point to point in mountainous terrain. On the last day of stress week candidates will walk a total of 40 miles (the long walk). Each selection class will start with as few as five and as many as 20 candidates. Each applicant must undergo and pass mental, physical, and physiological screenings. Of the 15–20 candidates who attend selection usually 5–7 will finish and usually only 50% of the ones who finish will actually be selected and have the opportunity to attend the 13-week-long LRRC training course, including free-fall training, technical skills in computers and signals, fieldcraft and stalks, infiltration and exfiltration methods, CQB-techniques, advanced driving techniques, marksmanship, demolitions, tactical man-tracking, and advanced medical techniques.

title: SYNTAC Airborne Medical Services
fluff: SYNTAC AMS/Blueberries/Blackberries/Winterberries
content:
Named ‘Blueberries’, ‘Blackberries’, and ‘Winterberries’ for the different colored ponchos they wear, SYNTAC was originally formed from SYNTEK’s foray into the PMC sphere providing ‘rapid airborne medical services’ under a program started by Arthur Anderson- co founder of the company. SYNTAC’s position within the SPB is the byproduct of the SYNTEK-Gold Coast Merger in 2019.  Defined by their different colored ponchos and SYNTEK blue pouches, gloves, and bands, SYNTAC conduct personnel recovery, hostage rescue, and combat search and recovery operations as well as other missions for Calamari’s clientele. Comprising of both paramedics and special operators, SYNTAC attach to other units across Calamari, UKSF, and SOCOM to conduct missions where appropriate. Ranging from leading hostage rescue missions, conducting combat search and rescue, and on demand emergency medical services.

As with the other units within the Special Purpose Battalion, SYNTAC’s training and selection is comparable to the units they hire the most from, USAF pararescue. However unlike their official counterpart within the USAF, SYNTAC primarily hire from the unit, and their training and selection is focused on brushing up skills. three months are spent in a mix of training and selection to ensure all candidates are up to the SYNTAC standard in both training and knowledge. The training includes courses in SERE, CQB-techniques, hostage rescue, free-fall training, man tracking, and EMT-Paramedic training. As well, all candidates undergo extensive medical, physical, and mental screenings before their final interview with the team they have been selected to join.

Teams usually consist of a small group in a Blackhawk that are intended to be in and out of an objective area, and focus on extracting wounded personnel. They usually comprise of:

- 2x Blackhawk Pilot and Co-pilot
- Lead and Assistant EMT (Often referred to as blueberries)
- 3-4x Medical Security (Often referred to as blackberries)

In addition, there are also dedicated medics in the backline- they are referred to as Winterberries, for their pure white ponchos.

These teams usually run on a rotation to allow them to rest, leading to leftover SYNTAC security and EMTs. Usually EMTs return to a medward to help where they can, or get RnR. However for blackberries they sometimes are requested for special missions and get attached to units within the R3 regiment or SRG. Oftentimes for these special missions, they function as medics, or help lead the team in the event of hostage rescue missions.

As of 2020, SYNTEK has moved select personnel from the SYNTAC branch to work in 3rd Special Reconaissance for Research and Development, and are working closely with medics across Calamari to standardize medical equipment and SOP.

title: Cyber Exploitation Group
fluff: CYEX
content:
During contracts in the Middle East after the debut of Gold Coast’s 3rd generation ARD datalinks- one of the main problems that arose was jamming and interference. In many cases, hostile groups were able to interfere with downlink connections from ARD systems to the CALLICOM netspace. And in incredibly rare instances- even the uplink. 

For these reasons, the Rapid Response Regiment organized members from their pre-existing signals unit and Gold Coast’s own Cybersecurity group to organize the Cyber Exploitation Group, nicknamed radioheads for the signalpacks that they carry. The main objectives of the group are to maintain the CALLICOM netspace and protect it from interference by eliminating whatever may be jamming signals, while also exploiting and interfering with enemy networks to add more ‘data’ into the datalink.

Unlike the other units within the Rapid Response Regiment, CYEX lacks the extensive selection course. Instead, their selection is more technical. Following the initial offer, new members to CYEX are put through an extra three months of training, ontop of R3’s standard training, for specific technologies and to work directly with Gold Coast to learn CYEX’s propreitary software- GoldenEye. Following training, most personnel are organized into hunter-killer teams with other units to eliminate interference at the source. In more recent times- CYEX has also moved towards cyberwarfare, with embedding units directly into LRRC or other frontline units to gather intel and run interference. 

As of 2021, CYEX members have also been seen embedded into Special Recon Groups for the same reason- but more permanently. With some members going through selection themselves and transferring their skills to the unit.

title: Joint NASA-ESA Satellite Missions reportedly 70% complete
fluff: By Jackie Watson. Published June 18th 2018
content:
(CNN)- In a press release this morning from NASA, satellite restoration missions in orbit are reportedly ‘70%’ complete. They are slated to become online in three weeks on the second anniversary of The Crash.

Before 2016, there were 1,459 satellites in orbit of the Earth. Information and statistics surrounding the amount lost have been inaccurate as more and more keep getting found in the atmosphere; however, with the mission 70% complete, NASA reported that only 100 satellites had survived the initial solar storm. Over eighty of them were unable to restore functions. In 2017 alone, hundreds of satellites were launched from both countries and the private sector to re-establish connections between people and countries. CNES reports the current statistic of only 861 satellites in orbit, almost all dedicated to communications and GPS.

Hundreds of astronauts have gone and returned from orbit, and NASA is coordinating with European Space Agencies to replace the current team in orbit soon. The team of 13 astronauts, comprising members from all across Europe and the United States, have been in space for over 340 days, setting records for the longest and most spacewalks during a single mission. As well as the VentureStar setting a new record for most consecutive deployments to low earth orbit in a row.

More satellite launches are also planned in the private sector, with Gold Coast and Aeromiro planning for their launches this year for different purposes. Gold Coast is launching its ‘Waypoint’ program. It plans to launch a thousand satellites over the next decade to provide high-speed, low-latency internet to areas with limited or unavailable infrastructure. Aeromiro is working with the SAPP on restoring observational satellites and has plans for a “Hubble 2” from what reports have mentioned.

title: Bartlett’s three year plan has cracks, tech sector struggles with lack of computer chips.
fluff: By Carter Olsen, FOX News. Published, June 24th, 2018
content:
(FOX) - Signs of strain are beginning to show only one year into President Bartlett's ambitious 'three-year' economic recovery plan. Initially hailed as a turning point for the U.S. economy after the 2016 Crash, concerns are mounting that the strategy may only be short-term relief.
﻿
A recent World Bank report warns that while emergency measures helped stabilize global markets, they also fueled rising public and private debt, which could derail a sustained recovery. Critics argue that Bartlett's approach has left the U.S. economy vulnerable, with unemployment still high at 8.6% and aid programs expiring. Many businesses, bracing for financial uncertainty, have already begun layoffs, deepening instability in a workforce still reeling from the crisis.
﻿
Beyond job losses, inflation and supply chain disruptions are still an issue. Manufacturing and energy costs are surging, forcing businesses to raise prices and slow growth. This is especially evident in the tech sector, which has been hit hardest by China's annexation of Taiwan and takeover of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). The resulting semiconductor shortage has crippled industries reliant on chips, from consumer electronics to automobiles. Apple and other tech giants have shifted to slower product cycles and raised prices, while U.S. and European efforts to boost domestic chip production remain sluggish.
﻿
Last week, Bartlett assured the public that the United States will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing to meet the rising demand to replace tech lost in the crash. However, with the Chinese CPU embargo and new domestic facilities in California and Texas years from full capacity, skepticism is growing over how his administration will deliver.

title: Crew 2 Astronauts Missing After Fault On Re-Entry
fluff: By Jackie Watson, CNN. Published June 26th, 2018
content:
Breaking (CNN) - NASA has reported in an unexpected turn of events that an ACS fault in the VentureStar upon re-entry has forced the 13 astronauts to veer off course. The space agency stated that they had landed off of the coast of Chile, but after a joint search between the United States and the SAPP, the astronauts could not be found. 
﻿
For the team of 13,  the last year has been long and enduring. Over a year was spent in space for them, and only today have they been able to make the journey home as another team was sent out to replace them on a mission to restore and deploy satellites in orbit. With over 70% of the work completed- primarily by the group of 13, Crew 2- they have set records for longest spacewalks, most concurrent spacewalks, and more. 

Crew 3 swapped with them this morning at 7am PST. However, from Nasa’s statement at 12:00 noon, the VentureStar suffered a fault and went wildly off course. The crew attempted to course correct, and satellites tracked them off the coast of Chile. However, when SAPP personnel arrived to help bring them back, what was found was that the ship looked ‘broken into’, and that there was a ‘forced entry’ according to SAPP officials who arrived to help the astronauts. 
﻿
SAPP sources claim that cartels had taken the astronauts hostage, specifically ‘La Unión Andina’, one of the three major cartels remaining in the SAPP’s efforts to curb Cartel activity within their territories. Since their announcement, the SAPP has promised to divert efforts to rescue the astronauts, but also justify a further budgetary increase for the SAPP’s military forces to combat the cartels 
﻿
The United States, UK, and Europe have all come forth stating similar information, and that they are pledging whatever they can to bring the 13 of Crew 2 home.

title: Military Lockdown Between Valparaiso and Santiago In Wake of Montecello Break In
fluff: By Irene Castro, El Pais. Published July 18th, 2018
content:
(El Pais) - Following the July 17th robbery of the Montecello Casino and Resort, local authorities along with Chilean Military have cordoned off the region with further lockdowns due to the increasing violence and presence of both mercenaries and cartels. 
﻿
The mayor of Valparaiso, Tomas Chandía, in a recent press conference following the lockdown order has stated that this is a 'temporary measure' to finally rout the Cartels from the region for good. However with many 'temporary measures' enacted by the SAPP, many citizens have voiced their complaints with a lack of results. When asked about how long these measures are to last, Mayor Chandía mentioned that they intend to keep these measures in place for the next month as anti-cartel operations 'come to a close' as he mentioned.
﻿
However what is lesser known, is outside of Valparaiso SAPP legislation has hired South African PMC, Klerk Solutions. Authorities have spoken very briefly on the subject during a conference in Brasília- where they said that these contractors were here to help fill 'operational gaps' for the SAPP because of the lockdown.

title: Turkey fomally votes to leave NATO
fluff: By Jackie Watson, CNN. Published December 20th, 2019
content:
(CNN) - Ever since the 2015 attempted Coup d'etat and the subsequent 2019 turkish offensive into Northeastern Syria, Turkey has had staunch relations with the United States and other NATO members. In recent times they have similarly moved to block entry of Finland, Sweden, and Ukraine into the alliance, and after recent reductions in funding to NATO's readiness- they have decided that NATO is no longer within their best interests. 
﻿
Today, Turkish foreign minister Cavasoglu arrived in Belgium to announce their immediate withdrawal from the alliance due to concerns of internal instability and direction. Citing that the alliance was a 'sinking ship'. 
﻿
President Bartlett has yet to make a statement on Turkey's immediate withdrawal, however many other NATO states have condemned Turkey for their actions in the July invasion of Northeastern Syria, and in the blocking of Finland, Sweden, and Ukraine from joining the alliance. However, in the wake of leaving the North Atlantic Treaty, rumors have risen on Russia offering a formal invitation to the CSTO as Tukic-Russo relations warm up. Especially with Russian Prime Minister Bukharov expressing support for Anti-Mercenary operations in Northern Syria.

title: Milford Adminidstration Makes Sweeping Changes To Foreign Policy
fluff: By Jackie Watson, CNN. Published January 30th, 2021
content:
(CNN) - Following the Inauguration of President Johannes Milford, his 6 month plan has been quick to spring into action. With massive spending cuts to countries overseas, such as Ukraine and Japan, and a promise made to the American public last year that they will 'stop wasting time with countries that don't want us'. French Prime Minister Leclerc has been very vocal in condemning Milford of leaving long standing allies behind with his statements on cutting all NATO spending. To which Milford has pointed out how France has done the same, and to 'not be a hypocrite'. 

However, while many celebrate a decrease in spending militarily- what Milford's administration has also been doing is cutting aid to countries abroad. Namely- in an abrupt move- all foreign aid to Japan, Ukraine, and the Middle East have stopped entirely. Leaving many countries relying on the food, supplies, and infrastructure the United States provided struggling to fill the gaps. 

Leaders in Europe have come forth as well to speak on the matter, with Germany's Prime Minister calling it a careless decision done in the name of cutting costs. Though at the same time, Milford has been making it a goal to become closer with the United Kingdom economically and militarily. Some in the United States have come to question if he's trying to join the commonwealth... And when asked during a press conference he laughed it off. He is set to arrive in the United Kingdom next week for a conference with British PM George Cowell and other leaders from Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

title: Broken Bones? Fixed In A Week
fluff: James McGill, FOX Sports. Published February 21st, 2021
content:
(FOX SPORTS) - SYNTEK medical technologies recenty had their "Chrysallis' Medical Nanites approved by the FDA for use in the United States. And with it, a legendary recovery over the last week in what most a few years ago would have called 'absurd' or 'fiction'. In the leadup to the 2021 Super Bowl, Pittsburgh Running Back Najee Harris had a major injury during the semifinal game agains the Jets. Breaking his ankle in what would have been a done and over season for him. However- with SYNTEK's Chrysalis Medical Nanites being approved just two weeks before- He was able to make a rapid, almost biblical recovery, over the last week to play in the Super Bowl this last weekend.

The Cost? Run an Advertisement with him afterwards, and with the Pittsburgh Steelers taking a landslide victory over the Raiders, the advertisement has made headlines as many consider Chrysalis to be a 'miracle drug'. An expensive one at that. 

Concerns have cropped up following the end of the season  on the ramifications of using nanomachines to speed up recovery times, and the concern is clear: Whose to stop 'recovery' nanites from becoming 'performance enhancing' in the field?

SYNTEK has refused to comment on the concerns during a confrence earlier this week in Seattle, but we managed to get in touch with the scientist behind it: Doctor Gabriella Gazzola. Gazzola mentioned that her work was specific to improving the human condition, and that she found it bemusing that it was being used in sports for this way. She did agree with the concerns however- as it is no secret SYNTEK does also create nanomachines for the military that are intended to improve performance as 'safer' steriods and stimulants.

However, one cannot help but imagine the work these miracle bots can achieve, and just how much of an impact they'll have on the post 2021 season.

title: A Cycle of Money And Control: Syria's Wild West
fluff: Jackie Watson, CNN. Published March 20th, 2021
content:
Even before the dancing lights of auroras lit up the skies and our internet vanished in hours, Syria was a mess of rival groups, contractors, and national militaries. Almost five years later, while the national militaries have left, militias and mercenaries participate in a secret, booming war economy in the north, while contras work to shut it down. 
﻿
It's a story shared across a large part of the Middle East, partly from the lack of support from the West and East. Countries such as Afghanistan, Syria, Iraq, and Iran stand as small villages and militias with what remains of the government, trying and failing to consolidate power and support. This power vacuum has opened the door wide for gunrunners, smugglers, and traffickers to treat the region as a 'wild west', where they can quickly store illicit goods out of sight of governments and other mercs, and then quickly transport them back out through ports in Egypt, Kuwait, and Iran. Local militias, however, have been quick to try and get in the way, leading to constant clashes in regions like northern Syria, where Russia and Turkey have spearheaded missions into the region in an attempt to stabilize borders and prevent these illegal goods from entering and leaving the 'black box'.
﻿
However, between those lines is the grey zone, where Contras operate. The UNCC has not been shy to hunt down members of the Blacklist wherever they can find them, using contras from BMF, Klerk, and Calamari and paying top dollar for those who bring mercs in alive. But in recent months, their missions have changed. Bounties from the UNCC and other neighboring governments have turned into anti-narcotics and anti-smuggling operations. Paying these contras top dollar for seizure of goods and supplies. 
﻿
"It's a bloody good job, mate. We get paid big money to bring in objectively bad people and stop drugs from making their way to Europe." One contra, who asked to remain anonymous, said. "Arguably I think I'm doing more here than I did when I was stationed in the region under Her Majesty."
﻿
Meanwhile, further south- Israel has been conducting raids deep into Iran and Syria in attempts to neutralize possible nuclear material refinement before they begin. However- they're not alone. Russian PMCs such as Dryga have been similarly conducting raids and seizing routes, becoming what locals refer to as 'warlords' in Russia's gambit to control the mining of Uranium and Lithium in Western Africa. All the while entering clashes with Israeli forces, Contras, and Mercs.
﻿
"These Russians are moving nuclear material through what is quite literally- a black box." Israeli Defense Minister, Natalia Hazan stated in an interview with CNN. "No one has control of the region, and without any foreign presence- we have to intervene."

title: Siberian Denuclearization leads to Insurgency
fluff: Jackie Watson, CNN. Published May 4th, 2021
content:
Two years ago during President Bartlett's administration, the newly formed Siberian republics made a deal to safely dispose and denuclearize once they had the facilities to safely do so. Said nuclear material was intended to become part of a new nuclear energy program for the newly formed nation, propped up by the United States and United Kingdom. However, in recent months under Milford's 6 month 'course correction' plan, the money for this program has stopped altogether, and while denuclearization efforts continue- reports have surfaced of a growing insurgency within the country. Set on making sure some of these nukes never get decommissioned. 

This insurgency primarily is headed by a sect of the Siberian armed forces, who have argued against denuclearization, believing it to be their only deterrent against a belligerent Russian Federation to their west, and a rising China to their south. And while they have allegiances to NATO allies such as France, who has sent nuclear engineers to assist with the development, they largely remain on their own. 

The Russian Federation has quickly come out to discuss the growing insurgency, citing that it is a threat to their national safety, and that the CSTO will not stand idle in the event that they secure nuclear weapons. Russian forces have been spotted amassing against the Urals, the natural border separating the two nations, in what has been described as a 'show of force'.
